name: Willa Bishop
life: “I still remember unraveling the last row of a very neat scarf.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Willa by a small Sunday habit. Willa starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I knitted her a retirement scarf with a loose end deliberately sticking out. I want her to come back and complain about my finishing.
appearance: Willa is easy to recognize by gray hair trimmed very close behind the ears and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Willa holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Willa is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To give the retiree a reason to come back and tease.
family: Harriet Chapman is Willa’s younger relative by marriage. Willa calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Harriet leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Harriet says, “I want my mother at home but can't lift her.”
connections: Teal Ruiz. An open window and a loose end of knitting make two invitations to come back in ordinary clothes.

reactions.situation: The successor asks for a private introduction at the door
reactions.response: Willa introduces the successor quietly and gives the client a chance to set the routine.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Willa separates the money question from the broken promise and asks which one the family wants to discuss first.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Willa thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
